guideSummary.surfnerd: South Bay is a beach break on Pingtan, also known as Haitan, the biggest island in Fujian and the fifth largest in China. Waves break over a mix of uneven reef and sand, and there are several surfable waves north and south of the big rock. A nice lefthander runs right beside the rocks, and righthanders show up in the middle of the bay once the huge 7 m tide drops out.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Haitan Bay (Haitan Dao) in Fujian is a reasonably exposed beach break that has fairly consistent surf. The best wind direction is from the east with some shelter here from southwest winds. Groundswells are more common than windswells and the best swell direction is from the north northeast. Waves at the beach are both lefts and rights. It very rarely gets crowded here. Dangerous rips are a hazard of surfing here.

guideSummary.surfnerd: 88 is a powerful left that peels over sand near a series of jetties in the Zhelang and Hong Hoi Wan area, generally the best bet around here. The jetties have shaped some excellent sand banks, with a left breaking off the northern jetty and clean A-frames setting up on the inside. There's history here too: the 2003 720 contest crowned Japan's Shinichi Yoshida as China's first surfing champion.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Hong Hai Bay (88) in Guangdong is an exposed beach break that has quite reliable surf and can work at any time of the year. Offshore winds blow from the northwest and there is no shelter here from cross shore breezes. Usually gets local windswells, but groundswells do happen and the best wave direction is from the south. Waves at the beach break both left and right. An uncrowded break, even when it is working. Be wary of rips - they make surfing here dangerous.

guideSummary.surfForecast: Riyue Bay (Riyuewan) in Hainan is a fairly exposed point break that has pretty consitent surf. Winter is the favoured time of year for surfing here. Good surf at all stages of the tide. A fairly popluar wave that can sometimes get crowded Watch out for dangerous rips.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Nanchangtu Bay is a fun beachbreak on Shengsi Island, throwing up punchy peaks over a sand bottom with the occasional barrel and waves peeling both left and right. It runs along a long sandy beach in front of Nanchang village, just across to the south of the island from Jinsha beach about 1.5 km away. Water quality here is poor, so it is worth rinsing off after a session.
